answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Amber polisher faceted gem mark witnessed by the lapidary guild flips the bet — each faceted gem is a wax seal pressed beside the cutters mark, so a farm must polish a hundred real ambers by hand — and the violet lands on the attacker instead. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the delta of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The island is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
